body: EBONY chats with Emmy-winning star Sheryl Lee Ralph about Abbott Elementary, her latest nomination, health advocacy, and why she sees many more seasons ahead. If you happen to be in a car accident the day before you speak with Sheryl Lee Ralph , this goddess of a woman is going to put you at ease. “Give yourself some grace. I applaud you for even carrying on with this interview. Thank you very much,” she stated so eloquently to this frazzled reporter. Car accident be damned, getting the opportunity to chat with Ms. Ralph isn’t something you give up easily. The star has been nominated for her fourth consecutive time for her work on Abbott Elementary , and she already has one win under her belt . Of course, she’s nothing but humble over her multiple nominations. “When I look at the group of women that are represented, it is a very diverse group,” she noted of this year's "Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy" category. “I’m happy to be a part of it and see this group the way we are together.” It seems everyone around the globe knows about Barbara Howard, the dedicated kindergarten teacher inside of the fictional Willard R. Abbott Elementary School in Philadelphia. “I was literally in Ghana—you have to picture this: I was canoeing up the river and we went to a rest stop, which means we literally pulled into a very small island where they were picking mangoes and coconuts and macheting them open and all of that,” Ralph recalled. “I was at this rest stop, and I am not exaggerating, when a little boy came over, stopped, put his hands on his hips, looked at me and said, ‘Ah, Abbott Elementary . ‘” And I was like, ‘Oh my God, the satellite is far reaching, and so is Abbott Elementary .” Speaking on the role she plays, Ralph shared, “Barbara has become a trusted voice for people; they actually listen to what Barbara says. I've had young women talk about how they wish they had a mentor like me. And they love the way that I actually care about Janine," (played by show creator Quinta Brunson). Ralph feels a sense of pride in showcasing teachers “in the light that they deserve as the wise ones…We always remember the best teacher that we had, and whether it is fictional or whatever, I'm very happy to be the world's favorite teacher.” Knowing she has that reach, Ralph has partnered with GSK to encourage people of all ages to live life to the fullest. “I'm so proud and happy to be able to partner with GSK and the THRIVE@50+ Campaign to raise awareness about shingles,” she shared. “When I was little, my grandmother developed shingles, and it was not pretty. When they tell you about a painful blistering rash, that's exactly what it is. And it was frightening. She had to stay in bed for quite some time. She wasn't around the family. And now the more I talk about this, the more people come out and say, ‘Whoa, I had it. And if I knew better, I would've done better. And that's why I am here to encourage people to get the information. Because if you are 50 or older, you've probably had chicken pox, which means you already have the virus inside you that leads you towards the possibility of developing shingles.” Ralph advises anyone over 50 to speak with their doctor about the disease and options for prevention. “Look, I'm getting ready for the Emmys, honey. I do not have time for that painful blistering…Do you remember when that lady said, ‘Ain't nobody got time for that. Ain't nobody got time for shingles.” What are three ways Ralph has improved her own health? “I can honestly tell you when your doctor tells you, drink your water. It seems so simple, but do you know how many people are walking around dehydrated? I have to remind myself all the time, drink your water,” she exclaimed. The actress advises moving more. “Get yourself a watch, a ring, something that says to you, get up out of that chair and keep it moving.” Under her doctor’s guidance, she shed 20 lbs. “Get rid of the physical weight. Get rid of the mental weight. Take care of yourself spiritually. Free yourself of some of the burdens,” she advised. “If you can prioritize yourself: talk to your doctor, talk to your pharmacist, you can get the proper information that you need to know about things like shingles and about the prevention of so many other diseases.” As for the comments from Brunson about it being harder for the cast to commit to so much time for the show, potentially preparing us for a possible end of Abbott Elementary with its upcoming fifth season, well, Ralph has something to say about that. “I'm always thinking of, we've got season five; what about season six and seven? I'm looking forward to seven seasons of Abbott Elementary , especially when I know it'll probably go on for 10,” she exclaimed. “One thing I learned a long time ago from a lot of the actors and mentors that came before me: you hold on to a good thing for as long as you can because sometimes the time between this good thing and the next greater thing can be a long time. Save your money so that you can start to create the projects that you would like to be a part of, so that you can uplift other voices and let them be heard the way you have been heard.” More wise words from the world's favorite TV teacher. The 77th Emmy Awards airs live Sunday, September 14, at 8 p.m. on CBS and Paramount+. Abbott Elementary, season five, premieres on ABC on Wednesday, October 1.

body: Nipsey Hussle’s spirit lives on not only in his music but in the business world. The late rapper passed away in 2019 at 33, as AFROTECH™ previously reported. His oldest brother, Blacc Sam, has played a pivotal role in ensuring “The Marathon Continues.” One example is The Marathon Clothing brand, which launched in 2009 and opened its flagship store in 2017 in the Crenshaw District of Los Angeles, according to a press release. Blacc Sam, as Nipsey Hussle’s business partner, revealed that his late brother’s children, Emani Asghedom and Kross Asghedom, would become owners of the clothing store. “When I say we own it, it’s in Hussle’s kids’ names, in their trust fund,” Blacc Sam told Rashad Bilal and Troy Millings, hosts of the “Earn Your Leisure” podcast. “When they get older, this is something their father worked for, and that they own, and that’s important to me. Also, just having a brick-and-mortar once again reinforced what Hussle told us and taught us.” He continued, “Just through the ups and downs of you know of whatever with business or brands, whether your shi-t boomin’ online and slows down, just having that brick-and-mortar and being able to pass it down through the family, I think is important.”   On Melrose Avenue, half a mile from that clothing store, exists another venture called Marathon Burger, Eater Los Angeles reported. It serves wings, Wagyu beef burgers, and shakes. It also offers vegan-friendly options, including a plant-based burger, a portobello mushroom burger, and a grilled vegetable salad, as AFROTECH™ previously reported. Blacc Sam manages the businesses and is, at times, hands-on in the kitchen, he shared with CBS News. He was inspired to open the business because he would cook in the kitchen with Nipsey Hussle during their childhood. “I think [the] Marathon brand, created by Hussle, was kind of like to inspire and to just motivate, and it just means to keep going,” he told the outlet. “It’s not a race, it’s a pace, do it on your own. … Anything that we can continue doing in that spirit is always a blessing.” Marathon Burger started as a pop-up in 2024 and expanded to locations on Melrose Avenue, Venice Beach, and Canoga Park in the Los Angeles area. Now, it is adding another location in Long Beach, CA, with a grand opening scheduled for March 1, according to information shared on its Instagram. The expansion is made possible through a partnership between Blacc Sam and the Broadus family, which includes Snoop Dogg and Cordell Broadus.
